audit.why: Both layers and the packet already read Zed on all seven rows, and that is right: Twisted Fate has no dash, no shield and no escape until Destiny at 6, while Zed's Q reaches 900 and his W enters from 650. The 50.48% aggregate over 4049 games reflects TF's global macro, not the duel — the page says as much in late and spikes[3].
audit.corrected: No chart edits proposed; the layers already agree.

audit.why: Zed's spikes are 3 (E online), 6 (Death Mark into a target with no durability) and first-item lethality. TF's spike is Destiny at 6, which is a map spike rather than a lane one, and the ratings already taper from 8/10 to 7/10 at two items to reflect it.
audit.corrected: Left as-is; the ratings already track the real curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pick a Card was treated as an ability that goes off when he casts it. It is an auto-attack modifier with an auto-reset: he picks the card, then the STUN arrives on his next basic attack. The page told you to watch the card glow, which is the wrong cue — the wind-up is the cue. Destiny revealing ALL enemy champions was also never stated, only that it 'gives vision for a gank'.
audit.why: Riot's W text: he chooses a magic card and uses it for his next attack. Riot's R text: reveals all enemy champions and enables Gate, a 1.5-second teleport.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dosFull[1].d, enemyWin and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that carries the numbers.
audit.corrected: Pick a Card a flat 6s, Wild Cards 6s to 5s, Destiny 170/140/110, Living Shadow 20s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability-name errors in content prose, plus two copy-paste bleeds. early said 'his blue Wild Card wave-clear', conflating Wild Cards (Q) with the blue Pick a Card (W). spikes[2] wrote 'Gold Card (W)' as if that were the ability name.
audit.why: Wild Cards and Pick a Card are two different abilities; gold and blue are colours of the latter.
audit.corrected: early now separates Wild Cards from the blue Pick a Card; spikes[2] now says 'Pick a Card's gold'. dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d replaced with bodies matching their titles.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Living Shadow (swap) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Pick a Card is a flat 6s, and the stun lands on his next basic attack — the wind-up is the tell, not the card flip. - Wild Cards is 6s to 5s. - Destiny is 170/140/110 and reveals every enemy, so assume he sees you the moment it hums. - Living Shadow is 20s.

edits.after: Q from 900, W the flank, E the slow — he has no dash, so a two-angle scissor lands whole on an immobile target.

edits.before: W wide, E the slow, Q the scissor from two angles — half a bar of geometry he answered by standing still wrong.
edits.after: Pick a Card resets in 6s — your free window is right after the card is spent, so trade then and step back out.

edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by locking a card before you commit, stunning your entry, and turning Destiny into a gank you never saw arrive.

edits.before: Ahead, audit the map: scissor Twisted Fate off every contact, mark the thresholds, and roam the crashes — fed Zed makes health bars legal documents.

edits.before: Level 1-2 you already control the lane: Twisted Fate is immobile with only Wild Cards to push and no way to punish you back, so you can walk up and Q him on cooldown while denying his CS. Watch for his blue Wild Card wave-clear letting him shove, but he pays for that push by giving you free step-up trades. Keep the wave near your side and chip him so he's low for a 6 all-in.
edits.after: Level 1-2 you already control the lane: Twisted Fate is immobile with only Wild Cards to push and no way to punish you back, so you can walk up and Q him on cooldown while denying his CS. Watch for Wild Cards and the blue Pick a Card clearing the wave, but he pays for that push by giving you free step-up trades. Keep the wave near your side and chip him so he's low for a 6 all-in.

edits.before: With Youmuu's you can dive TF under tower or catch him the instant he steps to farm; he must hold Gold Card (W) to survive, and you can W-dodge the stun then re-commit.
edits.after: With Youmuu's you can dive TF under tower or catch him the instant he steps to farm; he must hold Pick a Card's gold to survive, and you can W-dodge the stun then re-commit.

notes: The chart already agreed across both layers and the packet, so no chart edits were proposed. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Gold Card' and 'Wild Card' — the first was a real naming error (fixed to Pick a Card) and the second was a genuine conflation of Wild Cards (Q) with the blue Pick a Card (W), also fixed. Pick a Card's kit 'range: 200' is the card-select range and not his attack range, so I described the stun as arriving on his next basic attack without quoting a distance.
